newsitem.title: BRAZIL: MOTOR RACING-FITTIPALDI STILL UNDECIDED OVER RETIREMENT.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FITTIPALDI STILL UNDECIDED OVER RETIREMENT.

text.p: Former Formula One world champion Brazilian Emerson Fittipaldi, nearly killed in an American IndyCar crash two months ago, admitted on Saturday he had still not decided whether to retire.

The 49-year-old, who suffered severe neck and back injuries in the 180-mile an hour crash at Michigan in August, was speaking after making a visit to the Brazilian round of the FIA International Touring Car Championship at Interlagos as the guest of honour of Mercedes Benz.

"I feel quite good at the moment, I just need a lot of massaging on my neck," he said after sitting in the Mercedes Benz C-Class car that will be driven in Sunday's race by his nephew, former Grand Prix driver Christian Fittipaldi.
"That was the first time I have sat in a racing car since the crash and it was very emotional and very moving. It is great to be back at Interlagos again."
Fittipaldi echoed statements he had made immediately after the accident when he said he believed the crash was a message from God telling him to stop racing.

"I will have a medical examination in two months time to see how I am and only then will I consider my future," he said. "In my heart I want to drive now, but I have to think a lot about the decision.
"I got the message. I'm very religious and I believe a lot in God. I think it was a warning and I have to consider a lot for the future."
He also made it clear that IndyCar racing, which suffered the deaths of Americans Scott Brayton and Jeff Krosnoff in two separate crashes this year, needed to make continued improvements in safety.
"IndyCar racing is very safety conscious, and I think the safety has improved a lot recently because if my crash had happened four or five years ago I wouldn't have survived," he said.
"But although the safety is good, we are pulling 4Gs in some corners, which is too much. We must lower the downforce levels, because where I crashed we are doing 4.5G and that is far too much."
